model_annotation: The line graph illustrates the percentage of employed individuals (Anteil Erwerbstätige in %) across different age groups (Alter), categorized by migration background. The x-axis represents age, ranging from 20 to 70, while the y-axis shows the employment rate from 0% to 100%. Four distinct lines represent different groups: individuals without a migration background (black line), those born in Germany who are immigrants (gray line), those who immigrated before 2009 (light blue line), and those who immigrated since 2010 (dark blue line). The employment rate for all groups generally increases from age 20 to a peak around age 50, after which it declines. The black line, representing individuals without a migration background, consistently shows the highest employment rate, peaking at approximately 87% around age 50. The gray line, for those born in Germany, follows a similar trend but with slightly lower rates, peaking around 85%. The light blue line, for immigrants who arrived before 2009, starts at a lower rate (around 35% at age 20), rises to a peak of about 70% around age 50, and then declines. The dark blue line, for immigrants who arrived since 2010, shows a similar pattern but with lower employment rates overall, starting at around 38% at age 20, peaking at approximately 65% around age 50, and then declining sharply, falling below 10% by age 70.
